title: Contracts & Performance Obligations
description: Identify valid customer contracts and distinct promised goods or services.
html:
Step 1 — Identify the contract

Revenue accounting begins by determining whether an arrangement qualifies as a contract with a customer.

Important contract considerations

  • The parties have approved the arrangement.
  • The rights of the parties can be identified.
  • Payment terms can be identified.
  • The arrangement has commercial substance.
  • Collection of consideration is probable.

Step 2 — Identify performance obligations

A performance obligation is a promise to transfer a good or service to a customer.

Distinct goods or services

A contract may contain more than one promised good or service.

A promised good or service may be accounted for separately if it is distinct.

Example — Phone + Service

A telecommunications company enters into a contract that includes:

  • A smartphone
  • 12 months of wireless service

The company must evaluate whether these promises represent separate performance obligations.

Why performance obligations matter

If a contract contains multiple performance obligations, the transaction price may need to be allocated among them.

Revenue is then recognized as each performance obligation is satisfied.

Think ahead

One contract does not necessarily equal one revenue event.

A single contract can contain multiple separate promises that are recognized at different times.

quiz.prompt: A customer contract includes a product and a separate service. Why is identifying separate performance obligations important?

choices.text: Revenue may need to be allocated and recognized separately for each obligation
It means the customer never pays cash

quiz.explanation: Different performance obligations may receive different portions of the transaction price and may be satisfied at different times.
